cards.explanation: The answer is False. The text says the king of Arad hears Israel is coming along the road to Atharim, and he attacks Israel (Numbers 21:1). He's a Canaanite king who lived in the Negev. So no peaceful passing, friends. He attacked, and he captured some prisoners.

The answer is some prisoners, friends. The text says the king of Arad attacked Israel "…and captured some prisoners." That's all it tells us he took. Real people were taken, and I think that's why the next part matters so much.

The answer is that they make a vow to the LORD, bakers. After the attack, the text says "So Israel made a vow to the LORD…" (Numbers 21:2). They brought it to Him. Me, I'd have probably started by panicking at full volume. Israel makes a promise to the LORD.

The answer is that they ask the LORD to hand the people of Arad over to them, friends. Israel says, "If You will deliver this people into our hands…" (Numbers 21:2). Notice how the vow starts with "If." They're asking the LORD to deliver the people, and they attach a promise of their own to the request. The vow then goes on to say, "…we will devote their cities to destruction."
The answer is True, bakers. The text says, "…the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites." (Numbers 21:3). Israel asked, and the LORD heard it. That plea went somewhere.

The answer is that they keep it, friends. In the vow, Israel said, "…we will devote their cities to destruction." (Numbers 21:2). Then the LORD delivered up the Canaanites, and the text says "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction…" (Numbers 21:3). They said it, and then they did it. This is a heavy part, but the text is clear that the vow was kept.

The answer is Hormah, bakers! After the LORD heard Israel's plea and delivered up the Canaanites, the text says "so they named the place Hormah." Israel gave that spot a name it would carry from then on. That's one way to make sure nobody forgets what happened there. I put my name on my cookie planet the same way, though mine was carved into a handle by the Millers.
